title: Latency-aware SKU tiling & reserve optimizer (Hosted API unit econ)
summary: Working spreadsheet to evaluate per-model & per-region unit COGS for Hosted API with an emphasis on latency-driven SKU tiling and reserve commitments. Combines amortized infra, license, and caching effects to produce suggested per-token pricing bands and margin estimates. This is an early draft for ops/product discussion — contains assumptions and open questions for trade-offs between latency SLOs and reserve sizing.
notes:
Assumptions:
- Infra cost per token includes GPU runtime, networking egress amortized by observed tokens/sec distribution per SKU and region.
- License amortization is spread across expected token volume from committed capacity for each model family.
- Cache hit rates are rough estimates from trace samples (see linked artifact). Cache hits reduce effective infra time per req by ~40% on average.
- Latency targets: <100ms p95 for interactive small models, <200ms for large chat-optimized models (may need local reserve in EU for cross-region penalty).
Methodology:
1) Start with measured tokens/sec at p95 concurrency for each sku/region.
2) Convert infra cost per-hour into per-token via tokens/sec * 3600.
3) Add license amortization and subtract cache hit savings.
4) Compute suggested_price_per_token as 2.5x to 4x of effective_cogs based on strategic margin band for hosted tiers.
Open questions / risks:
- H100 pricing volatility in eu-west could swing margins by 10-15% in peak months. Need regional hedging.
- Bursty tail: our current reserve fraction (commit/peak) may underprovision for short spikes leading to fallback to more expensive on-demand.
- Quantized SKU performance variance across instance types needs more samples (RTX6000 vs A100-40GB).
